nodes.content: Design runtime verification for multicore embedded controllers that preserves deadline guarantees and sound verdicts despite asynchronous, lossy telemetry.
requirements: Verdicts are sound under telemetry loss and complete for bounded-response violations when telemetry is lossless.
Monitoring adds ≤5% worst-case execution time per control job while preserving all specified deadlines.

nodes.content: Use sequenced per-core logs, bounded-skew timestamps, gap-aware three-valued bounded-response monitors, and response-time-certified 5% instrumentation budgets.
What heartbeat period, delivery bound, and clock-skew limit permit sound violation finalization after a response deadline?
With 2 ms heartbeats, 1 ms delivery, and 100 µs skew, contiguous per-core watermarks soundly finalize violations within 3.2 ms.
Derive watermark closure bounds; simulate packet loss and skew to check unknown verdicts and 3.2 ms lossless finalization.
Simulate four-core WatermarkBench: 2 ms heartbeats, 1 ms delivery, 100 µs skew, injected loss; check soundness and closure.
WatermarkBench's 1 million trials yielded zero false violations under loss and detected every lossless violation within 3.2 ms.
Adopt contiguous per-core watermarks and unknown-on-gap verdicts; WatermarkBench met 3.2 ms closure with zero false violations.
Instrument controller jobs with the adopted watermark logger; measure WCET overhead and verify deadlines via multicore response-time analysis.
ControllerMonitor-v1 contains the per-core watermark logger, three-valued verifier, per-job WCET overhead measurements, and multicore deadline-analysis reports.
Replay 100,000 ControllerMonitor-v1 traces with 1-ms delivery, 100-µs skew, and burst loss; check lossless 3.2-ms closure and unknown-on-gap verdicts.
ControllerMonitor-v1 found 27 lossless violations finalized after 3.2 ms (maximum 3.38 ms) because relative clock skew reached 200 µs.
With relative skew bounded by 200 µs, contiguous watermarks finalize lossless violations within 3.4 ms; gaps remain unknown.
Replay ControllerMonitor-v1 traces at 200 µs relative skew and burst loss; verify 3.4 ms closure and unknown-on-gap verdicts.
In 100,000 ControllerMonitor-v1 replays, lossless closure peaked at 3.38 ms; unresolved lossy gaps yielded unknown, with zero false violations.
Does ControllerMonitor-v1 keep every control job’s measured WCET overhead ≤5% and multicore worst-case response time below its deadline?
Stress-test ControllerMonitor-v1 per-job WCET under cold caches and peak contention; compute overhead ratios and interference-aware deadline bounds.
WCET analysis under cold-cache contention bounded per-job instrumentation overhead at 4.6%; response-time analysis certified all deadlines with ≥0.7 ms slack.
Use DMA hardware trace and a dedicated core for gap-aware interval-timestamp monitors, with bus-interference-certified ≤5% control overhead.
Specify DMA sequence-gap and interval-timestamp semantics, then test verdict soundness, lossless violation completeness, bus interference, and deadline bounds.
Run TraceBusBench against ControllerMonitor-v1’s 4.6% WCET baseline, comparing lossy verdict soundness, lossless completeness, bus interference, and deadlines.
TraceBusBench report compares DMA and ControllerMonitor-v1 verdict accuracy, per-job WCET overhead, bus interference, and certified deadline slack.
Audit TraceBusBench’s report using 100,000 paired traces and cold-cache bus-contention schedules; recompute verdict errors, WCET overhead, and deadline slack.
TraceBusBench: zero unsound lossy verdicts, 100% lossless violation detection across 100,000 traces; maximum job overhead 2.8%, minimum slack 0.9 ms.
Adopt DMA tracing with contiguous-watermark, unknown-on-gap verdicts; TraceBusBench shows 2.8% maximum overhead and zero unsound verdicts.
Implement DMAMonitor-v2 on a dedicated core with sequence-gap detection, interval timestamps, contiguous watermarks, and per-job deadline certification.
DMAMonitor-v2 includes dedicated-core trace decoding, sequence-gap-aware bounded-response verdicts, interval-timestamp watermarks, and per-job WCET/deadline certificates.
Under 10 ms DMA-overflow bursts, gap-aware DMAMonitor-v2 yields zero false violations across 100,000 traces.
Inject 10 ms DMA-overflow bursts into 100,000 oracle-labeled DMAMonitor-v2 traces; count false violations and inspect gap-to-unknown transitions.
Eight false violations occurred in 100,000 traces: DMA overflow dropped responses before sequence assignment, hiding gaps and falsely closing watermarks.
Replay eight failing DMAMonitor-v2 seeds with pre-sequencing ingress counters; check whether overflow stays invisible to gap detection.
Existing DMAMonitor-v2 ingress counters marked all eight replayed overflows unknown; the earlier harness suppressed their interrupts, causing false verdicts.
Deploy per-core inline three-valued monitors before telemetry loss, exchanging epoch-tagged events through statically scheduled mailboxes with fixed instrumentation budgets.
Can four-core mailbox exchanges correlate cross-core responses before verdict deadlines while keeping each job’s WCET overhead ≤5%?
DMAMonitor-v2 with inline epoch-tagged mailboxes yields zero false violations under 10 ms overflows and deadline-safe cross-core correlation at ≤5% overhead.
Restore DMAMonitor-v2 overflow interrupts; benchmark four-core epoch-tagged mailboxes under 10 ms overflows for soundness, correlation latency, WCET, and deadlines.
Four-core replay found zero false violations, but mailbox contention raised worst-job WCET overhead to 6.3%, exceeding 5%.
In DMAMonitor-v2, replace 6.3%-overhead contended mailboxes with padded per-core slots; retest overflow soundness, correlation, WCET, and deadlines.
Padded-slot replay: zero false violations across 100,000 overflow traces, complete, timely lossless correlation, 4.7% peak overhead, 0.4 ms deadline slack.
Replacing contended mailboxes with padded per-core slots bounds overhead at 4.7% while retaining sound overflow verdicts and deadline-safe correlation.
Certify padded-slot mailbox latency under four-core contention, then bound per-job WCET overhead and response times against every deadline.
Analyze DMAMonitor-v2 padded-slot latency under four-core contention; verify ≤4.7% overhead, ≥0.4 ms slack, and sound overflow verdicts.
Four-core analysis bounded padded-slot latency at 0.18 ms, peak overhead at 4.7%, and minimum deadline slack at 0.4 ms.
Replay DMAMonitor-v2 with padded slots and enabled overflow interrupts; check gap-aware soundness and lossless correlation under 200 µs skew.
At 200 µs skew, padded-slot replay produced six false violations in 100,000 traces: overwritten cross-core responses evaded gap detection.
Defer padded-slot deployment: despite 4.7% overhead and 0.4 ms slack, undetected overwrites cause false violations; require overwrite-visible counters.
Add release-ordered per-core generation counters before padded-slot overwrites; replay six failing seeds and recertify overhead and deadlines.
DMAMonitor-v2.1 adds release-ordered overwrite counters; its validation bundle contains six-seed replay logs and updated WCET and deadline analyses.
Do DMAMonitor-v2.1’s overwrite counters prevent false verdicts under concurrent writes without exceeding 5% overhead or missing deadlines?
Stress DMAMonitor-v2.1 with concurrent slot overwrites and 10 ms telemetry loss; measure false verdicts, job overhead, and response-time slack.
DMAMonitor-v2.1 recorded zero false verdicts in 100,000 lossy traces, 100% lossless violation detection, 4.9% peak overhead, and 0.2 ms slack.
Use hardware event taps and timer-comparator shadow automata; sticky overflow flags force unknown, isolated-bus analysis certifies deadlines.
Specify shadow-automaton timing and sticky-overflow semantics; validate verdicts under loss and certify tap interference against 5% overhead and deadlines.
Port DMAMonitor-v2.1 bounded-response properties into timer-comparator shadow automata; add sticky tap-overflow flags and preserve epoch-tagged cross-core correlation.
ShadowTap-v1 contains timer-comparator automata, epoch-tagged cross-core event taps, sticky overflow registers, and job-interference analysis scripts.
Benchmark ShadowTap-v1 against DMAMonitor-v2.1’s 4.9% overhead, testing lossy verdicts, lossless violation detection, and deadline slack.
ShadowTap-v1 showed zero false violations across 100,000 lossy traces, 100% lossless detection, 1.6% peak overhead, and 0.8 ms deadline slack.
Prefer ShadowTap-v1 over DMAMonitor-v2.1: both passed verdict tests, but peak overhead fell from 4.9% to 1.6%.
Integrate ShadowTap-v1 into the four-core controller; run cold-cache interference tests and verify bounded-response verdicts under injected tap loss.
ShadowTap-v1 integration bundle contains four-core firmware, tap-loss replay traces, cold-cache interference measurements, and per-job deadline certificates.
